title: Access zoning & rate controls demo - Mariner Health
summary: Walkthrough of org/project key model for multi-tenant rate limiting, burst windows, and access zoning. Demoed policy configuration in Console, discussed audit logs/KMS for Private deployment, and agreed to run a 2-week pilot to validate burst behavior and billing segmentation.

Schedule pilot kickoff meeting for week of 12/15 (Dana + Alex)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Dec 08 2026 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Rivera (Redwood CSM); Dana Ruiz (Mariner Head of Platform), Samir Khan (Mariner SRE), Lena Moore (Mariner Security), Ethan Park (Mariner Dev)

Summary: quick demo of how org/project keys map to quotas and routing, with emphasis on burst behavior and auditability for a regulated healthcare workload.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um we'll do a 45-ish minute run through and then leave time for q&a, i am alex chen from redwood, with priya our se and jordan on success. who all do we have on the mariner side?
[00:12] Dana Ruiz: hey alex, dana here, samir and lena and ethan are on my side too. thanks for doing this. we're most interested in per-customer quotas and, uh, keeping PII out of logs.
[00:22] Priya Patel: great, thanks dana. quick agenda: show Console policy config, demo api/project key flows, talk about private deployment options for KMS and audit logs, and look at optimize suggestions for batching and quantization that affect unit costs. sound good?
[00:34] Samir Khan: yep that covers it. two things to flag up front: we run a ton of small requests from mobile apps so concurrency is a big one, and we also have predictable monthly spikes around midnight ET.
[00:45] Alex Chen: ok perfect, we can show quota slices and burst windows that map to your pattern. first here's the Console - i'm going to share my screen. (brief pause, screen share noise)
[01:10] Priya Patel: so in Console you can create an Org policy that sets baseline TPS and concurrent token limits per org, then attach Project keys for each client. the nice part is project keys inherit defaults but can have overrides - so you get both global guardrails and per-customer slos.
[01:30] Ethan Park: can we set different quotas for realtime vs batch endpoints? like low latency chat vs async embeddings?
[01:36] Priya Patel: yeah you can. we have route-level quotas - you can tag routes as chat/generate/embeddings and apply different rate windows. for example set a 100 rps chat limit but 500 rps async embeddings for the same project key.
[01:50] Lena Moore: about audit logs - if we go Redwood Private in a VPC, do logs ever leave our control? we need to show auditors chain of custody.
[01:59] Alex Chen: great question - for Private deployments audit logs are customer-managed, and we integrate with your KMS/HSM so keys never leave your vault. we'll send the SOC2 and architecture diagram after the call.
[02:10] Samir Khan: what about SSO and RBAC? we need fine-grained admin roles for dev vs ops.
[02:17] Priya Patel: we have SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC in Console supports role templates - Admin, Billing, Ops, ReadOnly - plus you can scope keys to projects so devs only see their project tokens.
[02:30] Alex Chen: i'll also note we have token-level cost tagging so you can map usage back to billing codes.
[02:36] Dana Ruiz: ok, show us the rate limit config UI and how we do burst handling.
[02:42] Priya Patel: sure. (clicking) here's an example org policy: base qps 50, concurrency 20, monthly quota 3M tokens. then you can add a burst profile - a 5m burst window that allows short-term exceed to 200 qps with token buckets.
[03:05] Priya Patel: the important bit is the system enforces both fairshare and sticky routing. so if a project bursts, we can route requests to cheaper model variants or to dedicated pools depending on your policy.
[03:18] Samir Khan: sticky routing - meaning a request from the same project will prefer the same instance to keep kv cache warm?
[03:24] Priya Patel: exactly. sticky lanes keep KV cache affinity which reduces latency for chat-style workloads. but if you want strict cost control we can bypass sticky routing and route to a quantized cheaper model variant.
[03:37] Ethan Park: what's the behavior if a project exceeds quota during a midnight spike - do we reject, queue, or degrade?
[03:43] Alex Chen: configurable: reject by 429, soft throttle with 10s backoff, or automatic downgrade to a fallback model. most customers pick soft throttle + fallback for user-facing features.
[03:52] Dana Ruiz: fallback concerns me for regulated data - if we downgrade to a different model, how is data handled and logged?
[03:58] Priya Patel: fallback models can be either our verified open models running in the same private environment or a quantized instance in a dedicated pool. data handling follows the same retention and KMS rules. we can also turn off fallback for sensitive routes.
[04:12] Samir Khan: any quirks with concurrency quotas and long-lived streaming sessions? we do a lot of streaming chat with token windows that last several minutes.
[04:20] Priya Patel: streaming counts toward concurrency buckets; we expose a streaming-concurrency metric and you can reserve a concurrency pool for streaming that's separate from short-lived generation calls. that prevents streaming sessions from starving sync requests.
[04:33] Alex Chen: i'll demo a quick policy change - watch project key "mariner-mobile-prod" get a new burst profile - notice instant enforcement in the control plane. (typing sounds)
[04:56] Priya Patel: now on the API side: you can send the project key in the headers or use org+project pair; SDKs support token rotation and automatic key pinning. note: for multi-tenant routing you should prefer project keys so you get per-customer accounting rather than sharing an org key across clients.
[05:20] Ethan Park: we have existing middleware that expects a single header per tenant. migrating is effort; can we do a hybrid?
[05:25] Alex Chen: yes, you can keep org-key at the edge and mint short-lived project tokens at auth time - Redwood has an endpoint for token minting and we have examples in the Quickstart. that preserves minimal changes in your edge services.
[05:40] Dana Ruiz: how do quotas map to billing? i.e. we want clear cost attribution per customer.
[05:46] Alex Chen: every project key emits token-level accounting. Console maps usage to billing codes and you can export csv or push to your billing export sink. you can also create quota-based alerts tied to cost meters.
[05:57] Priya Patel: also, Optimize module will suggest batching and quantizing for heavy workloads - often cuts unit cost by 30% with minimal quality loss. we can run a quality lift check against your prompts during the pilot.
[06:12] Samir Khan: latency SLAs - if we go hosted vs dedicated, what's realistic?
[06:18] Alex Chen: hosted API usually hits 50-150ms token latency on our fastest models in proximate regions. Dedicated with pinned GPUs and sticky routing can drop that to 20-60ms depending on prompt shapes. Private on-prem can match Dedicated but depends on your infra.
[06:33] Lena Moore: for compliance we need retained audit trails for 7 years - do you support that?
[06:40] Alex Chen: we support long-term retention via customer-managed log sinks for Private and Dedicated customers; we can ship logs to your S3/GCS or to our long-retention archive if contracted. we'll detail in the security pack.
[06:52] Dana Ruiz: ok let's try a scenario - Samir will simulate a midnight burst where 20% of tenants spike to 10x. what will happen?
[06:59] Samir Khan: yeah i'll run that internally - but priya, can you outline the expected enforcement path?
[07:05] Priya Patel: enforcement: (1) token-bucket burst allowed up to configured burst cap; (2) fallback routing to cheaper model variant if policy allows; (3) if still over limit then soft-throttle or reject; (4) alerts and a snapshot of KV heat-map for debugging. we'll capture those logs and show you the per-tenant distribution.
[07:22] Ethan Park: is there built-in anomaly detection for sudden quota exhaustion?
[07:26] Priya Patel: yes, Console has a detection rule you can enable that fires when usage exceeds a percentile baseline over X minutes. it can trigger webhooks or auto-scale recommendations.
[07:38] Alex Chen: quick note on quotas and plan controls - you can bind quota profiles to subscription plans so new projects inherit the plan limits automatically which helps with onboarding.
[07:49] Dana Ruiz: what's the recommended pilot size to validate both billing attribution and latency?
[07:53] Alex Chen: typically 10-20 clients across both chat and embeddings for 2 weeks, with one scheduled high-throughput test. that gives enough diversity to tune burst profiles.
[08:02] Priya Patel: i'll show the optimize suggestions now - this is the Evaluate tab where you can upload prompt sets and get regression alerts and quantization impact metrics. (screen click) the heatmap here shows prompts that are sensitive to lower-precision models.
[08:24] Samir Khan: ok good. can you also show the open api policy json? we want to store it in gitops.
[08:30] Priya Patel: yes, every policy can be exported as yaml/json. here's an example policy artifact that you can push to your repo and our control plane will pick up via CI webhook.
[08:42] Ethan Park: one more - for billing segmentation, can we map projects to internal chargeback codes?
[08:47] Alex Chen: absolutely; Console supports tags and you can configure billing exports to include those tags for ingestion into your finance system.
[08:55] Dana Ruiz: okay this has been helpful. two blocker questions: 1) can fallback models be restricted in Private so they run in our environment only? 2) what's the timeline/effort for token-minting integration?
[09:09] Priya Patel: 1) yes, fallback to private model variants is supported, you control which model families are allowed. 2) token minting integration is usually a day or two of engineering work; we have SDKs and reference middleware.
[09:23] Alex Chen: next steps recapped: alex sends security pack, we set up pilot template and pricing, samir runs a burst test, priya shares the recording.
[09:31] Dana Ruiz: sounds good. any questions from your side mariner?
[09:35] Lena Moore: only to confirm support windows and escalation path for Dedicated or Private - do we get 24/7 on-call for incidents?
[09:42] Alex Chen: Dedicated customers usually have an elevated SLA and 24/7 incident support depending on contract level; we'll include options in the pilot pricing doc.
[09:51] Samir Khan: ok thanks. we'll aim to have initial test results by the 14th.
[09:55] Alex Chen: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
[10:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: some proper nouns may be slightly off; timestamps approximated.
notes: Demo focused on policy configuration, fallback controls, private deployment auditability, and pilot plan. Customer prefers hybrid implementation with token minting and long retention. Recording to be provided.
